preamble: Affrication of the alveolar ejective fricative: [sʼ] is realized as the ejective affricate [tsʼ]. In Amharic the consonant written ጸ, with which ፀ (Geʽez ṣ́, from Proto-Semitic *ṣ́) has merged, is analysed as /sʼ/. Hayward & Hayward (1992: 51) state that /sʼ/ "is most commonly pronounced as an affricate, [tsʼ]", that it tends to merge with /tʼ/, especially word-initially, and that regional and sociolinguistic factors decide where the fricative survives; their speaker said [tsʼ] in /sʼəhaj/ 'sun'. Wiktionary transcriptions show both: ጻፈ 'to write' and ፀሐይ 'sun' with t͡sʼ, ሕፃን 'baby' with sʼ. The direction of the variation is not settled: Wikipedia's ejective article notes that Amharic is interpreted by many as having an ejective fricative [sʼ], at least historically, but has also been analysed as having it only as a sociolinguistic variant (Takkele Taddese 1992), and other atlas files treat Geʽez ጸ as [tsʼ]. In Hausa the variation goes the other way round, from /tsʼ/ to [sʼ] (see tsʼ > sʼ).

examples.note: Hayward & Hayward (1992: 49) give the word as sʼafə; Wiktionary transcribes it with the affricate.

Hayward & Hayward (1992: 51): their informant "consistently pronounced initial [ts'] in the word /s'əhaj/ 'sun'". ፀሐይ is a learned word from Geʽez (the native word is ጀምበር); Wiktionary lists ጣይ as a doublet, showing the merger with tʼ. Wiktionary gives ሕፃን 'baby' as /ˈhɨsʼan/, with the fricative.
